name: Molecular function established by identified inputs and outputs
description: Support a defined molecular effect through identified inputs and measured outputs of the actual protein/preparation, with assay competence, controls and conditions.

support.proposition: The actual source protein or preparation performs a specified conversion, transport, binding or physical effect on identified inputs under explicit conditions, with output identity and assay limitations retained.

A competent negative can weaken that proposition under those conditions; insolubility, missing substrate/partners, assay failure or contamination uncertainty leaves intrinsic capacity unresolved. Separate binding, proxy signal, net conversion and spontaneous downstream decomposition. observed_extent applies only to actual measured input/source geometry, clipped to original material; target_footprint can restrict that measurement. direct applies only when actual source subjects and the target proposition/conditions match. qualifications: Side activity does not establish ordinary native responsibility, and a tested panel does not establish universal exclusivity. A source-reported bound remains a bound, not zero or an exact numeric threshold measurement; use the existing typed bound field when recording a genuine source bound. No assay magnitude is converted into score confidence.

Retain actual source_ref, source_subject_refs, condition_refs and assumption_refs. The published examples below are instruction provenance about their named subjects; they are not observations of ybhP/b0790 and were not repeated to prepare this draft.

At construction and in decision context, resolve these observation kinds through annotation_support_routes for the actual caller-bound annotation policy; an entry does not supply universal component labels, select a projector, mask another kind, change a weight, or create a target finding. An unavailable route declaration remains unavailable.

Use actual retained assessments in a compatible annotation account. Selecting this entry earns nothing. The current caller-owned applicability × relation × extent arithmetic, same-component maximum, coherent-account integration and derived discrimination remain unchanged for this review basis. A finding qualification is not an automatic numeric discount; no independence, confidence or new score dimension is implied.
support.boundary: A reporter, affinity value, survival rescue or preparation contaminant does not automatically establish purified conversion. No assay-completeness or product-authentication threshold, assay-to-reliability function, or new experiment is adopted. Published preparations remain their source subjects when compared with the fixed target.

evidence.limit: Primary abstract/methods and initial context read; complete results not read in this pass.

evidence.observation: Docking favored adenine/adenosine compounds; biochemical assays supported MTA, SAH and adenosine but not AMP or SAM.
evidence.limit: Read relevant primary results and methods; live deposited binding-site API retrievals. Original API URLs lacking entity ID returned 404 and were repaired using current PDBe documentation. No repository changes or scientific-case runs.

evidence.observation: The matched M. voltae FlaB2 leader panel retained cleavage-flanking residues. FlaK processed lengths 12,10,9,8,7,5, but not 6,4,3; PibD processed all nine. Separately, M. maripaludis ΔflaK accumulated unprocessed membrane archaellins, lacked archaella/motility and retained pili. Native FlaK complementation restored processing and archaella/motility. Sulfolobus PibD gave an apparent processed-band shift at 37 °C, but no archaella or motility at either tested growth temperature.
evidence.limit: Qualitative published outcomes, complete relevant Methods/Results and bounded table audit; no wet-lab replication or direct native cleavage-site/topology measurement. | Source observation limit: FlaK panel assays used M. voltae membranes at 37 °C; PibD used E. coli membranes at 55 °C. Native complementation used a different methanogen, M. maripaludis. PibD was undetectable by anti-His, extracted membranes lacked detectable activity and cleavage termini were not mapped. Mislocalization, lipid dependence or missing assembly interactions remain hypotheses.

evidence.observation: Radiolabel incorporation and product analysis distinguish integration products from plasmid topoisomers. Band X is not radiolabelled and is interpreted through disintegration/topology experiments. Blocking both protospacer 3-prime hydroxyls prevents integration; Cas1 also catalyses disintegration of a defined half-site substrate.
evidence.limit: Three primary E. coli relevant Results/Methods inspected, with earlier other-species nuclease comparators explicitly limited; new descriptive deposited-coordinate comparison. No biological experiments or new annotation run. | Source observation limit: A change in plasmid migration is not automatically covalent spacer integration. Cas1's demonstrated integrase strand-transfer role must not be collapsed into an unsupported requirement that Cas1 or Cas2 cuts donor DNA to generate all prespacers.

evidence.observation: Authors: purified NlpI binds several endopeptidases; pairwise interactions alone do not establish simultaneous binding.
evidence.limit: Relevant full pull-down, affinity, ternary-complex, activity and synthase-association Results; scaffolding Discussion; corresponding MST/denaturation/complex/PG-digestion Methods inspected. Other proteomics/localization Methods not exhaustively read.

evidence.observation: UgtP amount and localization depend on nutrients/UDP-glucose pathway state. Mutants alter cell length. Purified UgtP inhibits FtsZ assembly, while localization changes are separable from gross protein abundance.
evidence.limit: Full Results on nutritional dependence, pathway controls and FtsZ assays inspected. | Group source-use limits: Cellular perturbations and purified FtsZ assays are connected study outputs, not independent proofs of every causal link. Native sensing remains bounded.

evidence.observation: YfgM alone did not reproduce PpiD anti-aggregation activity.
evidence.limit: 2014 primary full Results/Discussion and 2019 full primary article inspected. Detergent-dependent detection limits retained. | Group source-use limits: Detergent dependence limits association/negative assays. Later crosslinking repeats/extends complex detection; it is not independent functional activity evidence. | This row selects an exact clause from the aggregate retained observation; other source clauses are not attributed to this URL.

evidence.observation: Purified complex reduces ferredoxin only with crotonyl-CoA; omission controls and NADPH substitution distinguish dependencies.
evidence.limit: Full relevant introduction, purification/assay methods, results, tables and discussion inspected; raw HTML and parsed paragraphs saved.

evidence.observation: 8 mM malonyl-CoA gives only half the activity of 0.05 mM malonyl-ACP; other tested acyl-ACPs are inactive. Mass analysis supports methyl ester formation.
evidence.limit: Full relevant primary introduction, methods, all results and discussion inspected; source figure numerical constants not independently fitted.

evidence.observation: Thiol labeling/peptide MS detect reduced DsrC; derivatization/HPLC detects sulfide increasing with substrate. Recovery is only 40-50%, with quantitative limitations disclosed.
evidence.limit: Full relevant primary results, discussion, assay/product methods and limitations inspected; 2015 DsrAB source saw abstract only and is not counted as a separately verified case.

evidence.observation: 2022: changing only the downstream CofD/FbiA partner changes the apparent precursor preference. Cognate mycobacterial pairs favor PEP, Mycetohabitans pairs 3-PG, tested archaeal pairs 2-PL. GPPG is trapped structurally.
evidence.limit: Relevant full primary results/discussion and assay/LC-MS/crystallography methods inspected in all three papers. No new flux measurements, crystallographic refinement or spectrum fitting.

evidence.observation: 2015 Biochemistry: time-resolved/HPLC/MS assays of S. aureus HemQ establish sequential oxidative decarboxylation; excess peroxide also destroys product heme.
evidence.limit: Relevant primary body/results and main methods inspected for both; detailed supplementary purification protocols and later mechanistic revisions not checked.

evidence.observation: Combining NADH with enzymatically reduced native ferredoxin increases H2 formation; purified enzyme needs added FMN.
evidence.limit: Full relevant primary methods, donor/stoichiometry results and discussion inspected; original raw gas-chromatography data not reprocessed.

evidence.observation: Purified complex reduces ferredoxin almost completely with H2 only when heterodisulfide is supplied, beyond the uncoupled hydrogenase equilibrium.
evidence.limit: Relevant entire primary body, methods, results, limitations and figure legends inspected. Supporting-information raw data not independently analyzed.

evidence.observation: Recombinant NfnAB reduces ferredoxin with NADPH efficiently only with NAD+; NADP+ reduction by reduced ferredoxin depends on NADH.
evidence.limit: Relevant expression/reconstitution/assay methods, results, stoichiometry figures and discussion inspected; supplements not independently reanalyzed.

evidence.observation: Elemental/cofactor analysis supports two Fe-S clusters and one cobalamin; LC-MS measures oQ-to-Q conversion.
evidence.limit: Relevant purification, reconstitution, activity/complementation methods, cofactor results and EPR interpretation inspected; raw spectra not reprocessed.

evidence.observation: DMAP binds UbiX; tested DMAPP/IPP do not yield comparable binding/modification evidence. Reduced FMN plus DMAP produces a prenylated flavin identified by mass/spectroscopy.
evidence.limit: Relevant primary body and methods, including substrate tests, filtrate reconstitution and structure work, inspected.

evidence.observation: Purified recombinant RMJ07785 phosphorylated shikimate; RMJ01903 phosphorylated homoserine. Cross-substrate assays detected no overlapping activity. These assays establish specificity beyond pathway association.
evidence.limit: Complete main paper, genome-analysis methods, results, and substrate-assay methods read. No WIT reconstruction, alignment, or enzyme assay rerun. Historical WIT identifier retained without an unverified modern-locus mapping. | Group source-use limits: Related genome occurrences are not asserted independent tests. The historical WIT/gi identity is preserved without an invented modern locus mapping; none of the analyses was rerun.

evidence.observation: Many bioY loci associate with biotin biosynthesis/regulons, but only approximately one-third link to bioMN; some genomes lack obvious BioMN homologs. In heterologous E. coli, BioY alone transported biotin. Longer accumulation assays initially suggested BioMN dispensability; initial-rate substrate titrations showed the full system has greater affinity. BioM Walker-A mutation impaired efficient uptake.
evidence.limit: Comparative results, all transport/complex results, discussion, and assay/bioinformatics methods read from full paper. No membrane assay or phylogenetic reconstruction performed. | Group source-use limits: Heterologous uptake does not establish a native role across all BioY paralogs, so it is not assigned allele-linked native A109. Late accumulation and initial-rate readouts are related tests.

evidence.observation: Chemically required chelation, amidation, and reduction motivated searching for a matching gene grouping. Several methanogen clusters combine a type-II chelatase, MurF-like ligase, nitrogenase-like pair, and amidation enzyme. The M. barkeri MurF-like CfbB converted two candidate reduced intermediates; reduced enzyme concentration made the faster seco-F430 reaction discriminate the preferred substrate.
evidence.limit: Complete main cluster/enzyme results and relevant ligase methods read. Not all structural/spectroscopic supplementary detail inspected. Cfb letter assignments kept specific to this paper, avoiding conflation with the 2016 study. | Group source-use limits: Use the 2017 paper-specific CfbB letter assignment. Not all spectroscopy/structural supplements were inspected; upstream natural electron supply remains unknown.

evidence.observation: Context nominates an enzyme ensemble; anaerobic reconstitution, HPLC/MS, substrate comparisons and product NMR establish final ring formation. Natural electron supply for preceding reductases remained unresolved.
evidence.limit: Complete main cluster/enzyme results and relevant ligase methods read. Not all structural/spectroscopic supplementary detail inspected. Cfb letter assignments kept specific to this paper, avoiding conflation with the 2016 study. | Group source-use limits: Use the 2017 paper-specific CfbB letter assignment. Not all spectroscopy/structural supplements were inspected; upstream natural electron supply remains unknown.

evidence.observation: IP-dependent ADP production, 31P NMR, and mass spectrometry established ATP-dependent IP-to-IPP conversion. This did not establish the unidentified upstream decarboxylation step or its candidate gene.
evidence.limit: Complete primary methods/results and pathway caveats read. No assay or genomic analysis rerun; historical whole-pathway claims not promoted to a current confirmed pathway. | Group source-use limits: The proposed upstream decarboxylation and its gene remain unidentified; historical full-pathway reconstruction is not confirmed by the measured kinase reaction.

evidence.observation: Subsequent work found free (R)-beta-lysine is the efficient PoxA substrate and rescues a yjeK mutant phenotype.
evidence.limit: 2010 hypothesis/results/methods passages and complete 2011 main article read. Detailed 2011 supplementary methods not inspected. No new genome count, alignment, or assays. | Group source-use limits: The 2010 source is explicitly a hypothesis; the 2011 source is later discriminating evidence, not information available to the earlier investigation. evidence.observation: RibK and the wHTH-RibK fusion occupy complementary genomes. Conserved upstream motifs recur at riboflavin biosynthesis/uptake loci; Thermoplasma auxotrophs instead point toward an uptake target. Recombinant proteins bound predicted DNA sites, kinase assays produced FMN, and FMN disrupted DNA binding. Candidate operator positions suggested activation.
evidence.limit: Complete genomic reconstruction, dual-function results, evolutionary caveats, and relevant bioinformatics/DNA-binding/kinase methods read. Structure section not exhaustively inspected; no motif scan or assay repeated. | Group source-use limits: Native activation/sign was inferred from operator positions, not established with native genetics/transcriptomics; it is not A107 observed native regulation. Kinase and binding outputs are connected study measurements.

evidence.observation: Recombinant expression increased FMN; purified protein converted riboflavin to an HPLC/MS-confirmed FMN product. Donor comparisons established the preference for CTP. Neighborhoods do not determine the phosphate donor.
evidence.limit: Complete short primary paper and methods read. No ribB-neighborhood retrieval or enzymatic measurement repeated. | Group source-use limits: Auxotroph occurrence is compatible with salvage but does not measure native salvage flux. Fold, adjacency and assays remain connected evidence, not automatically independent.

evidence.limit: Primary introduction and results inspected by root.

evidence.observation: Authors measured fluoride flux, contrasted chloride flux, and recorded channel currents from reconstituted proteins.
evidence.limit: Primary full results/methods and correction inspected by root.

evidence.observation: HemK truncation removed RF1 methylation; HemK-enriched extracts methylated RF1/RF2, with GGQ-mutant substrate controls. The neighborhood nominates the substrate class; methylation and residue specificity require these measurements.
evidence.limit: Full primary main text retrieved; identification, gene-organization, methylation results and methods read. No independent prfA-neighborhood query, mutation, or assay.

evidence.observation: Authors found no oxygen consumption by purified active enzyme, then tested quinone reduction.
evidence.limit: Primary LhgO results, controls and limitations inspected by root.

evidence.limit: 2012 Results/Methods; 2016 MeDH Results/growth/glassware/assay methods and ExaF Results, tables and assay details. evidence.observation: Clean deletion abolished glycine-only carbon growth, strongly lowered gcs2 transcripts, and removed most broad expression changes reported from an older transposon strain. Promoter reporters responded to glycine; EMSAs established promoter binding.
evidence.limit: Main Results, growth and RNA-seq/accession Methods; live GSE76522 metadata: four RNA-seq samples, two WT/two deletion, SRA SRP068065. No reads reprocessed. | Group source-use limits: GEO metadata are custody/availability information, not an independent RNA-seq experiment. GcsR is a regulator, not a glycine-cleaving enzyme; direct ligand binding remains unknown.

evidence.observation: B. plebeius grew on porphyran, not tested agarose/carrageenan preparations; porphyran induced the examined PUL genes. Recombinant GH16B/GH86A cleaved native and purified porphyran with diagnostic products. A neighboring GH16A was agarolytic although intact cells did not grow on agarose.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant growth/PUL induction/ICE/enzyme Results and methods overview; no human dietary intervention, historical transfer experiment or new enzymology. | Group source-use limits: One study measures induced loci, recombinant reactions and whole-cell growth. No transfer event/donor or human dietary intervention was established; negative growth retains substrate-preparation scope.

evidence.limit: 2019 relevant full Results and culture methods; 2023 purification/kinetics/quinone Results and methods. evidence.observation: Fucose induced the locus and improved growth. Cj0486 restored E. coli fucP function; radiolabeled uptake was lost in its mutant. Piglet competition showed a defect. Poultry effects differed with inoculum, supplementation and competition versus single-strain infection.
evidence.limit: Primary Results/uptake Methods and both papers' poultry Results inspected; no universal chicken-negative or virulence-essential claim. | Group source-use limits: The original string combines two papers and host conditions; neither URL is asserted to independently support every composite clause. No universal chicken-negative or virulence-essential conclusion follows.

evidence.observation: Isotope tracing showed methylcitrate accumulation and downstream TCA depletion. Vitamin B12 rerouting restored survival without fully restoring growth; other supplements addressed growth limitations. Purified GlpX was inhibited by methylcitrate.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results and culture/extraction Methods; no isotope-flux recomputation. The 2005 infection paper was retrieved but remains an abstract-level auxiliary source here. | Group source-use limits: Metabolomics, rescue and GlpX assays are connected evidence; isotope flux was not recomputed. The auxiliary 2005 infection source remains abstract-only.

evidence.observation: malR deletion removed extra growth supported by maltose/dextrin but retained sucrose growth. Locus transcripts and malE reporters fell; reporter activation was restored by MalR coexpression. Purified MalR bound the promoter; adding maltose did not change binding in EMSA.
evidence.limit: Relevant Results including deletion, reporter rescue and sugar-independent DNA binding; growth/deletion/purification Methods inspected. | Group source-use limits: Growth, reporters and EMSA are related system measurements. Sugar-independent EMSA does not rule out every possible ligand-binding/sensing mechanism.

evidence.observation: BtsT transported radiolabeled pyruvate specifically; purified proteoliposomes demonstrated proton-coupled uptake. CstA-related mutant selection and extracellular depletion established an additional route. Cold-starved cells accumulated BtsT and rapidly imported pyruvate; sensing-network mutants failed resuscitation under tested conditions.
evidence.limit: Relevant main Results/transport Methods across three papers, including alternative-transporter and resuscitation controls. Grouped as one investigation, not three cases. | Group source-use limits: Three papers form one connected investigation. No new transport fitting occurred; YhjX specificity remains unresolved. The network resuscitation phenotype is not forced into allele-linked BtsT-only A109.

evidence.observation: A markerless C260V substitution removed excitation quenching in purified IsiA. Under stringent iron deficiency and high light, mutant cells initially grew quickly then bleached/declined; low light avoided bleaching. In iron-replete high light the mutant reached greater density.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant mutant/spectroscopy/growth Results and growth conditions. No new fluorescence-lifetime analysis. | Group source-use limits: Spectroscopy and growth are connected but distinct measurements. Early and late outcomes do not independently support one unconditional benefit; no new lifetime analysis was done.

evidence.observation: Anoxically enriched activity reduced vinyl chloride/DCEs, not PCE and only slowly TCE. Peptide sequencing mapped the major candidate to vcrA; transcripts occurred in VC-grown cultures. Environmental water contained vcrAB DNA.
evidence.limit: Main purification/substrate/gene-identification/transcription Results and cultivation/assay Methods. GenBank AY322364 reported; no new field dechlorination or sequence analysis. | Group source-use limits: Culture was nonaxenic and protein only partially purified; there was no knockout. Activity, identity and transcripts are connected evidence, not independent proof of unique gene causation.

evidence.observation: Purified PA0142 was tested against a library exceeding 50 potential substrates; it deaminated 8-oxoguanine to urate.
evidence.limit: Primary paper abstract, target-selection narrative, substrate assay and concluding limitation inspected. Homolog crystal structure was not mislabeled as PA0142's own structure.

evidence.observation: Authors: purified PxpR binds 5-OP by ITC; four related amino acids show no detectable binding under tested conditions.
evidence.limit: Indexed complete relevant regulatory Results, transport Discussion, figure descriptions and culture/purification Methods inspected. Direct publisher fetch 403; raw binding data not obtained. Current published 2026 article used, not 2025 preprint.

evidence.observation: NADPH-dependent turnover yielded product matching authentic preQ1 by HPLC and proton NMR.
evidence.limit: Primary Results and Discussion plus alignment and assay descriptions inspected through indexed full-text sections. No sequence alignment or experiments rerun here.

evidence.observation: E43A preserved hya affinity approximately but expanded apo-protein recognition to a type-1 site. Symmetrizing the type-1 dinucleotide alone did not restore wild-type apo binding.
evidence.limit: Five primary papers’ relevant complete paths inspected as itemized in sources. One independent published-table/oligo arithmetic probe was run. No biological experiment, new regulon scan, raw-curve fit or IscR structure computation.
